steps: A key advantage of the Von Neumann architecture is the stored-program concept.
Both data and instructions are stored in the same memory.
This makes a computer flexible because programs can be changed or replaced without changing the hardware.
items.finalAnswer: The stored-program concept allows data and instructions to share memory, making the computer flexible and easy to reprogram.

steps: A computing system requires hardware, the physical parts of the computer.
It requires software, the programs and instructions that tell the hardware what to do.
It also requires data to be processed into useful information.
items.finalAnswer: The three main requirements are hardware, software, and data.

steps: A system is a set of interrelated components that work together to achieve a common objective.
The components are the parts or elements of the system.
The relationships between components allow them to work together.
The objective is the purpose or goal for which the system is designed.
The environment is everything outside the system that can affect it or be affected by it.
A system receives input from its environment, processes it, and produces output.
The boundary separates a system from its environment; an interface is the point through which the system interacts with its environment or another system.
Components communicate and exchange information through suitable links, signals, or interfaces.
items.finalAnswer: A system is a set of interrelated components that work together to achieve an objective and interact with their environment.

steps: Natural systems occur in nature and are not created by human beings.
They may be living, such as the human body or an ecosystem, or non-living, such as the solar system.
Natural systems perform functions according to natural laws and processes.
Artificial systems are designed and made by human beings to achieve particular objectives.
Examples of artificial systems include a computer system, a transport system, and a school system.
An artificial system has components arranged to perform its intended functions; it may be changed or improved by people.
items.finalAnswer: Natural systems occur in nature, while artificial systems are designed by people to achieve specific objectives.

steps: Natural science studies natural systems and the laws that govern them.
For example, biology studies living systems such as the human body, while astronomy studies systems such as the solar system.
Design science creates or improves artificial systems to meet human needs.
For example, engineers use system concepts to design and improve a transport system.
Computer science studies computing systems, including computers, software, and networks.
For example, a computer system can be studied in terms of its components, their relationships, its inputs, and its outputs.
System theory helps each branch identify components and relationships, understand how a system works, and improve its performance.
items.finalAnswer: System theory helps natural science understand nature, design science create and improve systems, and computer science study computing systems.

steps: A computer is an electronic system that accepts data, processes it according to instructions, and produces information.
A software system is a collection of programs and related data that performs specific tasks.
A computer network is a group of connected computers and devices that communicate and share data and resources.
The Internet is a worldwide network of interconnected computer networks.
These computing systems can work together; for example, a computer can use software to access information through a network and the Internet.
items.finalAnswer: Computing systems include computers, software systems, computer networks, and the Internet.

steps: A computer system is an artificial system designed to process data and produce useful information.
Its main objective is to accept input, process data, store data or information, and provide output.
Its main components include hardware, software, data, and users.
Hardware includes the input devices, processor, memory and storage devices, and output devices.
Software provides the instructions that control the hardware and perform tasks.
The user supplies data and instructions and uses the results produced by the computer.

The components interact: input devices send data to the computer, the processor follows software instructions to process it, memory or storage holds data and results, and output devices present the information to the user.
items.finalAnswer: A computer system uses hardware, software, data, and users to process input and produce useful information.

steps: The Von Neumann architecture is a computer design in which data and instructions are stored in the same memory.
The main components are the memory unit, the central processing unit (CPU), and input and output devices.
The memory unit stores data and instructions.
The CPU consists of the arithmetic and logic unit (ALU), the control unit (CU), and registers.
The ALU performs arithmetic calculations and logical operations.
The CU controls and coordinates the activities of the computer.
Registers temporarily hold data, instructions, and results during processing.
Input devices enter data and instructions; output devices present the processed information.
First, a program and its data are loaded into memory.
The CPU fetches an instruction from memory.
The CU decodes the instruction and directs the required operation.
The CPU executes the instruction, using the ALU when a calculation or logical operation is needed.
The result is stored in a register or memory, or sent to an output device.
The fetch-decode-execute process repeats until the program is completed.
items.finalAnswer: The Von Neumann architecture stores data and instructions in the same memory and processes instructions through the fetch-decode-execute cycle.
